info.title: Amplitude Public APIs
info.summary: Event ingestion, analytics, taxonomy, export, async DSAR jobs, and agent-readable site content APIs for Amplitude.
info.description:
Amplitude is a digital analytics platform covering product analytics, experimentation, session replay, web analytics, and CDP capabilities.

This document describes the public HTTP surface most useful to programmatic clients and AI agents:

- **Ingestion** (`api2.amplitude.com`) — send events. Authenticated with a project API key in the request body.
- **Analytics, Taxonomy, Export, Cohorts** (`amplitude.com/api`) — read and manage project data. Authenticated with HTTP Basic using a project API key and secret key.
- **DSAR** (`amplitude.com/api/2/dsar`) — export a user’s data. Authenticated with HTTP Basic using the organization API key and organization secret key, not project credentials.
- **Site content** (`amplitude.com`) — Markdown and index representations of amplitude.com pages, for retrieval-augmented and agent use.

For conversational access to Amplitude data, prefer the Amplitude MCP server (`https://mcp.amplitude.com/mcp`, OAuth 2.0) over these REST APIs. For public documentation, use the read-only Docs MCP server (`https://amplitude.com/docs/api/mcp`).

The full catalog of Amplitude’s agent-callable resources is published at https://amplitude.com/.well-known/ai-catalog.json.

Endpoint coverage here is deliberately limited to documented, stable endpoints. See https://amplitude.com/docs/apis for the complete reference, including the Experiment, Attribution, Lookup Table, and User Privacy APIs.

x-api-versioning.description: API families use independent path namespaces (for example /2/httpapi, /api/2/dsar and /api/5/cohorts). Batch and site-content paths are unversioned. The namespace number is not a shared release number or a semantic-version guarantee.

deprecationPolicy.description: No company-wide REST retirement notice period or sunset dates are asserted by this document. SDK maintenance policy does not establish REST API lifecycle policy.

tags.description: Model Context Protocol endpoint. Preferred over the REST endpoints for conversational and agent access, because it carries per-user OAuth scopes rather than a project-wide key pair.

post.description:
JSON-RPC 2.0 over Streamable HTTP, per the Model Context Protocol specification. Described here so the OAuth scopes an agent needs are discoverable from this document; the request and response bodies are defined by MCP, not by Amplitude.

Do not hardcode tool names — call `tools/list` and read the definitions the server returns at runtime.

`mcp:read` is sufficient for read-only tools. Tools that create or modify dashboards, notebooks, experiments, cohorts, or metrics additionally require `mcp:write`.

schema.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 request as defined by MCP.

200.description: JSON-RPC result, or an SSE stream when the client accepts `text/event-stream`.

401.description: Missing, expired, or revoked access token. The `WWW-Authenticate` header carries the protected resource metadata URL. Refresh once; if that fails, restart the authorization code flow.

403.description: The token is valid but lacks the scope for this tool, or the underlying Amplitude user lacks permission on the target resource.

servers.description: Event ingestion host (default / US data residency)

post.description:
Send events to Amplitude in real time. Requests are limited to 1 MB.

**Retrying safely.** Idempotency is per event, not per request, and is keyed on `insert_id` — Amplitude does not honour an `Idempotency-Key` header. Set a stable `insert_id` on every event before the first attempt and reuse it verbatim on retries; Amplitude discards an event whose `insert_id` matches one already seen for that `device_id` within the last 7 days. Without it, a retry after a network timeout double-counts every event in the payload, because a request that timed out may still have been ingested.

servers.description: Event ingestion host (default / US data residency)

post.description:
Upload large volumes of event data at once. Same payload shape as HTTP V2 with higher throughput limits and looser throttling. Use this for backfills and server-to-server pipelines.

**Retrying safely.** As with HTTP V2, idempotency is keyed on each event’s `insert_id` rather than an `Idempotency-Key` header. Backfills are the case where this matters most: a retried batch without stable `insert_id` values silently duplicates every event it contains.

get.description: Return every active and inactive event type in the project, with display name and deleted state.
Return metrics for one or two events over a date range, optionally segmented and grouped. URL-encode special characters in event types and property names.

parameters.name: e2
parameters.description: Second event definition, same shape as `e`.

parameters.description: First date included in the data series, formatted YYYYMMDD.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Last date included in the data series, formatted YYYYMMDD.

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: Metric to return. Non-property metrics: `uniques`, `totals`, `pct_dau`, `average`. Property metrics: `histogram`, `sums`, `value_avg`.

parameters.name: i
parameters.description: Interval: 1 for daily, 7 for weekly, 30 for monthly. Use -300000, -3600000 for realtime intervals.

parameters.name: s
parameters.description: Segment definitions, as a JSON array of filter condition objects. Repeat the parameter for multiple segments.

parameters.name: g
parameters.description: Property to group by, for example `platform`. Available only with a single segment. Limit: two.

parameters.description: Number of group-by values returned. Max 1000.

parameters.name: end

parameters.description: Set to 1 to include user properties in the export.

get.description: Poll while HTTP 202 reports JOB INPROGRESS. Download only after HTTP 200 reports JOB COMPLETED.

202.description: Export is still running; continue polling.

get.description: Redirects to a short-lived download link. The request URL is valid for seven days; each generated link is valid for one minute.

schema.description: Cohort data; the published reference does not specify a serialization format.

post.description: Submit a data subject access request. HTTP 202 returns requestId; poll getDsarRequestStatus until status is done or failed. Jobs complete within three days and results expire after two days. Requests do not include Statsig data.

202.description: Request accepted. Use requestId to poll for completion.

get.summary: Poll a data subject access request
get.description: Poll staging/submitted jobs. Stop polling on failed and inspect failReason; on done download the returned URLs with the same credentials before they expire. The documented cost budget is 14,400/hour: each POST costs 8 and each GET costs 1.

200.description: Request status, with download URLs populated when done.

get.description: Use an output URL returned by getDsarRequestStatus after status is done. outputId is the integer at the end of that URL. Links expire after two days. Clients may follow a redirect to the gzipped file; each file contains newline-delimited JSON events.

200.description: OpenAPI description of Amplitude’s public APIs.

orgApiKeyAndSecretKey.description: DSAR uses HTTP Basic with the org API key and org secret key, as documented in the DSAR request examples.

apiKeyAndSecretKey.description:
HTTP Basic authentication. Username is the project API key, password is the project secret key. Both are found in Amplitude under Settings → Projects → General. Credentials must be base64 encoded.

This scheme is project-scoped and all-or-nothing: a key pair grants every operation on its project. There is no narrower grant. When an agent needs least-privilege access, prefer the MCP server and its `mcpOAuth` scopes over these keys.

mcpOAuth.description:
OAuth 2.1 authorization code flow with PKCE, used by the Amplitude MCP server at `https://mcp.amplitude.com/mcp`.

Endpoints and scopes here mirror the authorization server metadata at https://mcp.amplitude.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, which is authoritative. Clients may be registered dynamically (RFC 7591) at `https://mcp.amplitude.com/register`; public clients are supported.

Scopes bound the token but do not widen it — every call is additionally enforced against the permissions of the Amplitude user who approved the grant. Request the narrowest scope that covers the task.

For EU data residency, substitute `https://mcp.eu.amplitude.com`.

scopes.mcp:read: Read charts, dashboards, cohorts, experiments, feature flags, events, properties, and session replays.
scopes.mcp:write: Create and modify dashboards, notebooks, experiments, cohorts, and metrics.
scopes.offline_access: Issue a refresh token so the agent can act after the user closes the browser. Omit for one-shot interactive tasks.

expires.description: Expiry date as supplied by the API.

min_id_length.description: Overrides the default minimum length of 5 for `user_id` and `device_id`.

Event.description: One of `user_id` or `device_id` is required, in addition to `event_type`.

event_type.description: Unique identifier for the event. `$identify` and `$groupidentify` are reserved for identification.

user_id.description: ID for the user. Minimum 5 characters unless overridden with `min_id_length`.

time.description: Event timestamp in milliseconds since epoch. Defaults to upload time.

event_properties.description: Data sent along with the event. Max depth 40.

user_properties.description: Data tied to the user. Supports `$set`, `$setOnce`, `$add`, `$append`, and `$unset` when `event_type` is `$identify`.

groups.description: Event-level groups. Requires the Accounts add-on. Up to 5 group types and 10 group values per event.

group_properties.description: Properties tied to the groups in `groups`. Applies when `event_type` is `$groupidentify`.

insert_id.description: Idempotency key for this event. Amplitude discards an event whose `insert_id` matches one already received for the same `device_id` within the last 7 days. Generate it before the first send — deterministically from the event, or as a UUID stored with it — and reuse the same value on every retry. Generating a fresh one per attempt defeats deduplication entirely.

session_id.description: Session start time in milliseconds since epoch. `-1` means no session.

event_id.description: Incrementing counter that distinguishes events with the same user and timestamp.

ip.description: IP address of the user. Use `$remote` to use the request IP.

user_agent.description: Unparsed user agent string, which Amplitude parses into user properties.

revenue.description: Revenue amount. When price and quantity are both sent, revenue is price × quantity.

events_ingested.description: Number of events ingested from the request.

payload_size_bytes.description: Size of the upload payload in bytes.

server_upload_time.description: Milliseconds since epoch when Amplitude accepted the request.

SiteContentError.description: Error response from the amplitude.com site content endpoints. Fields follow RFC 9457 problem details, extended with `code` and `hint`. Served as `application/json`.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

status.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

code.description: Stable machine-readable identifier. Branch on this rather than on `title` or `detail`, which may be reworded.

detail.description: What went wrong with this specific request.

hint.description: How to resolve it — whether to fix the request, look elsewhere, or retry.

instance.description: Path of the request that failed, when known.

ApiError.description: Shared description of existing error bodies, not a new wire envelope. JSON APIs may return optional code/error fields or an errors array; other endpoints return text or Markdown. Fields are optional and clients must use the HTTP status and Content-Type. Endpoint-specific details may be present.

code.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

examples: Invalid field values on some events

missing_field.description: Request-level required field that is missing.

events_with_invalid_fields.description: Maps field names to the indexes of the events that failed validation.

events_with_missing_fields.description: Maps field names to the indexes of the events missing them.

eps_threshold.description: Current events-per-second threshold for the project.

throttled_devices.description: Maps device IDs to their current events-per-second rate.

throttled_events.description: Indexes of events that were throttled.

silenced_events.description: Indexes of events whose device was silenced.

exceeded_daily_quota_devices.description: Maps device or user IDs to their daily event count, for those over quota.

IngestionError.description: Object-form ingestion error. ApiError is the shared response model.

DsarRateLimited.description: DSAR cost budget exceeded. POST costs 8, GET costs 1; all endpoints share 14,400 cost/hour. Reduce polling frequency before retrying.

IngestionBadRequest.description: Invalid upload request: malformed JSON, missing required fields, invalid field values, or silenced devices.

IngestionForbidden.description: Blocked by Amplitude’s web application firewall, or sent from a sanctioned region.

IngestionPayloadTooLarge.description: Payload exceeds 1 MB. Split the events array across multiple requests.

IngestionRateLimited.description: Too many requests for a user or device. Pause sending for that user or device for 30 seconds, then retry until the 429 clears.

example.error: Too many requests for some devices and users

example.title: Missing required parameter
example.detail: No page path was supplied. Append .md to a page path, for example /pricing.md.
example.hint: Request a page path, for example https://amplitude.com/pricing.md.

SiteContentServerError.description: The Markdown rendering could not be generated. Retryable.

example.title: Markdown rendering failed
example.detail: The Markdown rendering of /pricing could not be generated.
example.hint: Retry the request. If it keeps failing, fetch the page as HTML without the .md suffix.

AnalyticsBadRequest.description: Invalid request. Check that JSON query parameters are well formed and that special characters are URL encoded.

AnalyticsUnauthorized.description: Missing or invalid credentials. Send HTTP Basic auth with the project API key as the username and the secret key as the password.

AnalyticsRateLimited.description: Concurrent or hourly rate limit exceeded for the project. The response identifies which limit was hit. Up to 5 concurrent requests are allowed across Amplitude REST endpoints.
